A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PlaceIt3D and PlaceWizard. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary materials support comparison. Appendix content can be matched across renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark comparisons and component ablations in Table 2, plus predicted placements and confidence visualizations in Figures 4 and 6.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark results for PlaceWizard, its ablations, and two placement baselines in Table 2, alongside qualitative predictions.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same spatial pooling, asset encoding, three prediction heads, losses, and inference procedure. Figure 3 newly illustrates head internals, but neither the text nor the appendices establish an actual change to the proposed architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions use ScanNet scenes and PartObjaverse-Tiny assets for the same indoor placement task and spatial, rotational, and visibility constraints. The reported scene and asset counts remain unchanged. Revised sample counts and constraint mixtures do not establish new task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Section 5.1 and Table 2 add OpenMask3D + LLM, using GPT-4o with an estimated scene graph. OpenMask3D + rules and the Reason3D-derived comparisons remain. This is one additional comparator within the existing benchmark.

E3.justification: Reported training/validation/benchmark sizes change from 97,020/2,619/3,300 to 100,505/2,566/3,500, with revised constraint distributions. Section 3.2 changes the stated physical check from Open3D intersection testing to trimesh intersection and surface-support checks, and introduces Language Adherence Success. These substantially revise the reported evaluation conditions; appendix training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 4 revises the qualitative success and failure cases, expanding from six to eight examples with different prompts and placements. This changes the illustrative evidence about constraint satisfaction and errors. The A–G component-ablation design and appendix pooling and confidence-map analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Table 2 continues to report point estimates. The retained confidence heatmaps depict model predictions rather than uncertainty in experimental estimates.

E6.justification: Table 2 substantially revises existing scores and adds physical, visibility, language-adherence, and GPT-4o-baseline results. For example, PlaceWizard's reported spatial/rotational scores change from 54.1/12.1 to 56.6/17.3, while reported complete success changes from 29.4 to 15.0. These are revised benchmark outcomes under changed samples and checking procedures, not controlled performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: Section 3.2.2 defines a distinct evaluation quantity, Language Adherence Success, as the percentage satisfying every language constraint while excluding physical plausibility. This adds a mathematical metric definition. The placement parameterization, simplifying assumptions, and Equations (1)–(4) remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction refine the novelty claim around jointly handling placement ambiguity, geometric reasoning, scene–asset–language understanding, and noisy reconstructions without privileged test-time metadata. They explicitly acknowledge overlap with synthetic scene generation. The central benchmark, dataset, and PlaceWizard contributions remain.

C2.justification: V2 attributes the LLM baseline's physical failures to lacking direct geometry access and contrasts this with costly mesh-based checks. It interprets low complete-success scores as evidence of task difficulty. Section 6 additionally acknowledges that automatic annotations lack human verification, limiting annotation quality and evaluation reliability.

D1.justification: Figure 3 adds mask- and rotation-head implementation diagrams; Section 5.1 identifies GPT-4o and its scene-graph input; and the stated checking library changes to trimesh. V1's approximately 10,000 single-CPU-hour dataset-generation estimate is removed. Appendix hardware, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, training duration, and pooling settings are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands the placement and scene-generation lineage, adding furniture-layout optimization, WordsEye, text-to-3D methods, ATISS, LayoutGPT/LayoutVLM, Holodeck, and other work. The paper's positioning now emphasizes how reconstructed, metadata-free placement differs from synthetic layout generation, substantially broadening the earlier discussion.

P1.justification: The abstract, substantial portions of the introduction and related work, benchmark explanations, experimental discussion, limitations, and conclusion are rewritten. The introduction organizes challenges into four explicit items, and naming distinguishes PLACEIT3D-benchmark from PLACEIT3D-dataset. Method prose and supplementary content are comparatively stable.

P2.justification: Key displays are substantially reworked: Table 2 expands from four to seven metric columns and adds a baseline row; Figure 3 adds detailed head diagrams; and Figure 4 becomes an eight-panel montage with revised examples and annotations. Main-text displays are relocated, while appendix Figures 5–8 retain their content.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the evaluation more informative by separating physical feasibility from language adherence and adding a GPT-4o comparator. Broader prior-work coverage and explicit acknowledgment of unverified automatic annotations better qualify the contribution and its limitations. These improve interpretability and scientific context, although the new baseline remains briefly specified and changed evaluation conditions prevent a same-setting performance conclusion.
